summary: The automation send path re-derives the flag itself instead of calling the resolver. packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:246-248, :274-276 and :433-435 each compute `const brandingDisabled = reminder.booking.eventType?.team ? !!reminder.booking.eventType?.team?.hideBranding : !!reminder.booking.user?.hideBranding;` and pass it as isBrandingDisabled into the templates — reading only the team's own column or the organizer user's own column, so an organization that set hideBranding on the parent org is ignored. The data to do better is not even loaded: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/getWorkflowReminders.ts:198-203 selects `team: { parentId: true, hideBranding: true }` (parentId, but not parent.hideBranding) and :167-171 selects the user's bare hideBranding with no profiles.organization. The canonical rule lives at packages/features/profile/lib/hideBranding.ts:35-45 (resolveHideBranding — organization override wins) with the org-aware loaders at packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts:1323-1334 and packages/features/ee/teams/repositories/TeamRepository.ts:462-471. The page the customer books from does obey it: apps/web/server/lib/[user]/[type]/getServerSideProps.ts:299 (shouldHideBrandingForUserEvent), apps/web/lib/team/[slug]/[type]/getServerSideProps.tsx:199 (shouldHideBrandingForTeamEvent), apps/web/modules/bookings/views/bookings-single-view.getServerSideProps.tsx:253 and packages/features/ee/payments/pages/payment.tsx:58 (shouldHideBrandingForEvent) — hence the mismatch. The scheduling side is wrong the same way at every entry point, via an owner-only Prisma select: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/getEventTypesFromDB.ts:109-113 and packages/features/bookings/lib/payment/getBooking.ts:37-43 select `owner: { select: { hideBranding: true } }` only, and the value is passed as `!!...eventType?.owner?.hideBranding` at packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:2618,:2793,:2808, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleConfirmation.ts:459,:472 (selects at :309-313,:359-363), packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:471, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleBookingRequested.ts:112, packages/features/handleMarkNoShow.ts:377, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:561, packages/app-store/_utils/payments/handlePaymentSuccess.ts:230, packages/features/ee/round-robin/roundRobinManualReassignment.ts:671 (and a hardcoded `hideBranding: true` at :604) and packages/features/ee/managed-event-types/reassignment/services/ManagedEventManualReassignmentService.ts:188 — all of which yield false for team event types, whose owner is null. The workflow services do call the resolver but key it on the wrong entity: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/service/EmailWorkflowService.ts:90-92 and packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/service/WorkflowService.ts:133-135 pass the workflow's/form's own userId/teamId, not the booked event's. The flag is finally consumed where the vendor name is emitted: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/templates/emailReminderTemplate.ts:82-83, packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/templates/emailRatingTemplate.ts:79-80 and packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/templates/customTemplate.ts:216, each rendering `${t("scheduling_by")} ${APP_NAME}` unless isBrandingDisabled.
